facts.q: visa british uk passport 90 days stay how long entry tourist
facts.t: British visitors can stay up to 90 days in any 180 without a visa, for holidays, family visits, business meetings and events. Work has separate rules. Other passports: check your own government's travel advice.

facts.q: passport valid validity expiry months issued 10 years blank page
facts.t: A British passport must have been issued less than 10 years before you arrive and be valid for at least 3 months after the day you leave, with a blank page for stamps.

facts.q: schengen ees entry exit system fingerprints stamp border
facts.t: Cyprus is not in the Schengen area, so days here don't count towards the Schengen 90 days. The new EU Entry/Exit System (fingerprints and photos) does not apply in Cyprus. Passports are still stamped, so check you get a stamp on the way in and out.

src.t: Cyprus Mail, 23 Feb 2026: Schengen rules will not apply to Cyprus

facts.q: schengen join joining 2027 when
facts.t: Cyprus is working towards joining Schengen, with 1 July 2027 named as the target. Until it happens, nothing changes for visitors.

src.t: Cyprus Mail, 12 Nov 2026: Schengen target of 1 July

facts.q: ghic ehic health card insurance doctor hospital nhs
facts.t: UK visitors need a GHIC or EHIC for medically necessary state healthcare. It doesn't replace travel insurance: it won't cover private clinics or getting flown home.

facts.q: ehic cost doctor gp a&e emergency prescription ambulance free pay
facts.t: With an EHIC, a state GP visit costs €3, a specialist €6, an A&E visit €10 and each prescribed medicine €0.50 at a state pharmacy. Ambulances are free when you show the card. Hospital admission is through a state A&E or a public-system doctor's referral.

facts.q: heat heatwave hot sun summer sunstroke children car
facts.t: In a heatwave the Health Ministry advises staying out of the sun from 11:00 to 17:00, drinking water even when you're not thirsty, and never leaving children or pets in a parked car, even for a few minutes.

src.t: Politis, 14 Jul 2026: Health Ministry heat advice

facts.q: tap water drink drinking safe bottled
facts.t: Limassol's water board says its tap water meets EU drinking water standards. Many people still buy bottled water for the taste.

src.t: Limassol Water Board: water supply FAQ

facts.q: sea water clean quality bathing blue flag
facts.t: All 123 monitored bathing sites in Cyprus were rated "excellent" for water quality in the 2025 EU report.

src.t: Cyprus Mail, 16 Jun 2026: all bathing waters excellent

facts.q: lifeguard lifeguards hours safe swim season tower
facts.t: Lifeguards are mainly on duty from June to September and hours vary by beach. Around Ayia Napa and Protaras most towers run from about 9:30 to 17:00, and four beaches are covered from 7:00 to 18:30 in summer. No lifeguard on duty means you swim at your own risk.

facts.q: turtle turtles lara toxeftra akamas nesting sunbed umbrella
facts.t: Lara and Toxeftra in Akamas are turtle nesting beaches. From 1 June to 30 September there are no umbrellas, sunbeds or tents, and no staying on the beach from an hour before sunset. Driving on the sand is banned all year.

src.t: Cyprus Mail, 16 May 2025: turtle nesting rules

facts.q: drinking age alcohol legal age 18 bar served
facts.t: You must be 18 to buy or be served alcohol.

src.t: Business in Cyprus: alcoholic drinks trade

facts.q: smoking smoke cigarette vape indoors bar club fine car
facts.t: Smoking is banned indoors in bars, clubs and other enclosed public places, and in a car with anyone under 18. The on-the-spot fine for a smoker is €85. Smoking outdoors and on terraces is allowed.

facts.q: e-scooter scooter electric helmet age rent
facts.t: E-scooter riders must be 17 or over (raised from 14 in May 2026) and wear a fastened helmet. Scooters are allowed on roads with a 30 km/h limit and on cycle lanes, never in pedestrian areas. Police can impound them.

src.t: ROADPOL: Cyprus personal mobility devices law

facts.q: drone drones fly flying dji filming
facts.t: Drones are allowed again after a full ban from March to May 2026. EU rules apply: stay below 120 m and keep it in sight. Keep away from airports, military areas, the British bases, archaeological sites and any wildfire. Rules can change at short notice, so check with the Department of Civil Aviation before you fly.

src.t: Cyprus Mail, 12 May 2026: drone ban lifted
Cyprus Mail, 27 Aug 2025: no drones near wildfires

facts.q: time zone gmt clock hours ahead
facts.t: Cyprus time is GMT+2, and the clocks go forward an hour in summer.

src.t: Visit Cyprus: time and working hours

facts.q: shop shops opening hours sunday supermarket open siesta
facts.t: Some shops take a break from 14:00 to 17:00 between 15 June and 31 August. On Sundays shops open later, usually around 11:00. In tourist areas shops and supermarkets stay open late and open on Sundays. Banks, shops and public services close on public holidays.

src.t: Visit Cyprus: time and working hours

facts.q: language english greek speak words phrases hello thank you
facts.t: Greek and Turkish are the official languages and English is widely spoken. A few words go a long way: kalimera (good morning), yia sas (hello), efharisto (thank you), parakalo (please).

src.t: Cyprus Mail: customs and useful words

facts.q: church monastery dress code wear shoulders knees kykkos visit
facts.t: Dress modestly in churches and monasteries, with shoulders and knees covered.

src.t: Cyprus Mail: customs and useful words

facts.q: roaming phone mobile data sim ee o2 vodafone three
facts.t: UK networks can charge for roaming in Cyprus. As of April 2026, EE charges £2.59 a day, Three £2 and Vodafone £2.57. O2, giffgaff, iD Mobile, Smarty and Tesco include EU roaming. Check your own plan before you fly.

facts.q: best time visit when go month season spring autumn summer winter swim warm
facts.t: The sea is 24°C or warmer from June to October, peaking at 27°C in August and September. July and August are the hottest months, with daytime highs around 33°C on the coast. May and October are warm without the peak heat, and November still has a 22°C sea. Winter is mild and green, with snow on Troodos from about January.

src.t: Cyprus Department of Meteorology averages, via Wikipedia: Climate of Cyprus

facts.q: area where stay base nightlife party clubs bars young groups lively
facts.t: For nightlife, stay in Ayia Napa. It's the island's best-known nightlife strip, with the clubs and bars close together around the centre.

facts.q: area where stay base family families kids children toddlers young
facts.t: For families with young kids, Protaras and Ayia Napa work best: calm sandy bays, shallow water, waterparks in summer and the Ocean Aquarium.

facts.q: area where stay base culture history museums mosaics archaeology
facts.t: For culture and history, base yourself in Paphos (mosaics, Tombs of the Kings, the harbour) or Nicosia (the Cyprus Museum and the old city inside the Venetian walls).

facts.q: area where stay base no car without car car-free bus walk walking
facts.t: Without a car, the easiest bases are Kato Paphos, central Larnaca, Ayia Napa and central Protaras, where the beach, food and buses are a short walk away. A car really helps for the Troodos villages, Akamas and hill villas.

src.t: Our guide: where to stay without a car

facts.q: area where stay base quiet nature peaceful remote couples walking hiking
facts.t: For quiet and nature, stay around Polis and Latchi: Akamas walks, the Blue Lagoon boat trips and wild beaches like Lara.

src.t: Our area page: Polis, Latchi and Akamas
Our guide: Blue Lagoon boat trips

facts.q: area where stay base city food wine restaurants shopping marina
facts.t: For a city break with food and wine, Limassol has the old port, the marina, a long seafront and the wine villages in the hills behind it.

src.t: Our guide: things to do in Limassol

facts.q: area where stay base mountains cool winter snow troodos hiking villages
facts.t: For mountains and cooler air, stay in the Troodos villages: cool in July and August, and snow from about January.

facts.q: village villages omodos wine village limassol troodos
facts.t: Omodos (Limassol wine villages, 800 m): a cobbled square, a medieval wine press and Timios Stavros monastery. Known for wine, zivania and arkatena bread, with a big Holy Cross fair every 14 September.

facts.q: village villages lefkara lace silver larnaca
facts.t: Lefkara (Larnaca hills, 650 m): famous for lace embroidery and silver filigree, which you can watch being made. Festival every August.

facts.q: village villages kakopetria troodos solea old quarter
facts.t: Kakopetria (Troodos, Solea Valley): a protected old quarter of stone alleys, a 1754 watermill, and the painted church of Agios Nikolaos tis Stegis 5 km away.

facts.q: village villages kalopanagiotis kalopanayiotis marathasa troodos
facts.t: Kalopanagiotis (Troodos, Marathasa Valley): sulphur springs, a Venetian bridge and the UNESCO-listed Agios Ioannis Lampadistis monastery.

facts.q: village villages agros roses rose pitsilia
facts.t: Agros (Pitsilia, 1,100 m): rose growing and rose oil distilling you can watch, plus lountza, hiromeri and homemade sweets.

facts.q: village villages fikardou pitsilia nicosia monument
facts.t: Fikardou (Pitsilia, 900 m): the whole village was declared an ancient monument in 1978, with two house museums of rural life. Machairas monastery is under 15 minutes away.

facts.q: village villages lofou limassol grape festival
facts.t: Lofou (Limassol hills, 780 m): old stone architecture, an 1842 village tap, and a grape festival at the end of September.

facts.q: village villages lania artists limassol colourful
facts.t: Lania (Troodos foothills, Limassol district): cobbled streets, flower-covered stone houses, artists' studios and old wine jars.

facts.q: village villages pissouri halloumi limassol coast
facts.t: Pissouri (Limassol coast, near Cape Aspro): a hillside village known for halloumi and sweet sultana grapes, with old carob stores turned into restaurants.

facts.q: village villages tochni larnaca stone cycling
facts.t: Tochni (Larnaca district): one of the oldest villages on the island, built of local stone, with a small Byzantine museum. Good for cycling and horse riding.

facts.q: village villages kathikas paphos wine donkey easter
facts.t: Kathikas (Paphos hills, about 700 m): century-old houses, wineries, a small donkey sanctuary, and an Easter Passion procession on Good Friday.

facts.q: history historical neolithic stone age first settlers choirokoitia prehistoric
facts.t: Neolithic (from 11,500 BC): The first permanent settlements on the island. See it at Choirokoitia, UNESCO listed.
facts.what: The first permanent settlements on the island.

src.t: Deputy Ministry of Tourism: Cyprus, 11,000 years of history and civilisation

facts.q: history historical chalcolithic copper idol
facts.t: Chalcolithic (3900 to 2500 BC): Small-scale copper mining begins. See it at Cyprus Museum, Nicosia.

src.t: Deputy Ministry of Tourism: Cyprus, 11,000 years of history and civilisation

facts.q: history historical bronze age copper trade
facts.t: Bronze Age (2500 to 1050 BC): Copper working and trade across the eastern Mediterranean. See it at Cyprus Museum, Nicosia.
facts.what: Copper working and trade across the eastern Mediterranean.

src.t: Deputy Ministry of Tourism: Cyprus, 11,000 years of history and civilisation

facts.q: history historical mycenaean greeks city kingdoms phoenicians kition
facts.t: Mycenaean Greeks and city kingdoms (from the 13th century BC): Greek settlers arrive, and Phoenicians later settle at Kition. See it at Kition, Larnaca.
facts.what: Greek settlers arrive, and Phoenicians later settle at Kition.

src.t: Deputy Ministry of Tourism: Cyprus, 11,000 years of history and civilisation

facts.q: history historical archaic classical persian kingdoms tamassos evagoras
facts.t: Archaic and Classical (1050 to 312 BC): Independent city kingdoms, then Persian rule. See it at Tamassos Royal Tombs.
facts.what: Independent city kingdoms, then Persian rule.

src.t: Deputy Ministry of Tourism: Cyprus, 11,000 years of history and civilisation

facts.q: history historical hellenistic ptolemy alexander
facts.t: Hellenistic (310 to 30 BC): Ruled by the Ptolemies after Alexander the Great. See it at Pierides Museum.
facts.what: Ruled by the Ptolemies after Alexander the Great.

src.t: Deputy Ministry of Tourism: Cyprus, 11,000 years of history and civilisation

facts.q: history historical roman romans mosaics paul barnabas christianity
facts.t: Roman (30 BC to 395 AD): Paul and Barnabas bring Christianity in 45 AD. See it at Paphos Mosaics.
facts.what: Paul and Barnabas bring Christianity in 45 AD.

src.t: Deputy Ministry of Tourism: Cyprus, 11,000 years of history and civilisation

facts.q: history historical byzantine painted churches frescoes
facts.t: Byzantine (395 to 1191): The Church of Cyprus is independent, and the painted churches are built. See it at Troodos painted churches, UNESCO listed.
facts.what: The Church of Cyprus is independent, and the painted churches are built.

src.t: Deputy Ministry of Tourism: Cyprus, 11,000 years of history and civilisation

facts.q: history historical richard lionheart templars crusades berengaria
facts.t: Richard the Lionheart (1191 to 1192): Richard conquers Cyprus in 1191 and sells it to the Knights Templar. See it at Limassol Medieval Castle.
facts.what: Richard conquers Cyprus in 1191 and sells it to the Knights Templar.

src.t: Deputy Ministry of Tourism: Cyprus, 11,000 years of history and civilisation

facts.q: history historical lusignan frankish medieval kings
facts.t: Lusignan (1192 to 1489): Three centuries of Frankish kings. See it at Royal Chapel at Pyrga.

src.t: Deputy Ministry of Tourism: Cyprus, 11,000 years of history and civilisation

facts.q: history historical venetian venice walls caterina cornaro
facts.t: Venetian (1489 to 1571): Venice takes over and builds the great walls. See it at Nicosia's Venetian Walls and Famagusta Gate.
facts.what: Venice takes over and builds the great walls.
facts.see: Nicosia's Venetian Walls and Famagusta Gate

src.t: Deputy Ministry of Tourism: Cyprus, 11,000 years of history and civilisation

facts.q: history historical ottoman turkish rule 1571
facts.t: Ottoman (1571 to 1878): Ottoman rule. See it at Hala Sultan Tekke, Larnaca.

src.t: Deputy Ministry of Tourism: Cyprus, 11,000 years of history and civilisation

facts.q: history historical british britain colony
facts.t: British (1878 to 1960): Cyprus passes to Britain. See it at Cyprus Museum building, Nicosia.

src.t: Deputy Ministry of Tourism: Cyprus, 11,000 years of history and civilisation

facts.q: history historical independence 1960 republic
facts.t: Independence (16 August 1960): The Republic of Cyprus is proclaimed. See it at Liberty Monument, Nicosia.
facts.what: The Republic of Cyprus is proclaimed.

src.t: Deputy Ministry of Tourism: Cyprus, 11,000 years of history and civilisation

facts.q: history historical 1974 invasion coup division divided north green line
facts.t: 1974 (July 1974): A coup backed by the military junta then ruling Greece, followed by the Turkish invasion. The island has been divided since. See it at Byzantine Museum, Nicosia.
facts.what: A coup backed by the military junta then ruling Greece, followed by the Turkish invasion. The island has been divided since.

src.t: Deputy Ministry of Tourism: Cyprus, 11,000 years of history and civilisation

facts.q: history historical eu european union 2004 euro
facts.t: European Union (1 May 2004): Cyprus joins the European Union.

facts.q: living resident expat residence eu citizen yellow slip meu1 register registration move moving live
facts.t: EU citizens staying more than three months must apply for a registration certificate (form MEU1, the "yellow slip") within four months of arriving. The fee is €20 and the certificate has no expiry date. Documents must be officially translated and certified.

src.t: Civil Registry and Migration Department: EU citizens

facts.q: living resident expat residence eu stay longer three months work insurance conditions
facts.t: To stay longer than three months, an EU citizen must be working or self-employed, or have enough money and full health insurance.

src.t: Civil Registry and Migration Department: EU citizens

facts.q: living resident expat uk british residence permit brexit move moving live visa longer than 90 days
facts.t: UK nationals who move to Cyprus now and stay longer than 90 days must apply for temporary residency as non-EU nationals. Permanent residency may be possible after five years or more.

facts.q: living resident expat uk british brexit withdrawal agreement already living before
facts.t: UK nationals and their families who were already living in Cyprus under EU free movement rules before Brexit keep their rights to live and work here under the Withdrawal Agreement.

src.t: Civil Registry and Migration Department: UK nationals

facts.q: living resident expat gesy ghs healthcare health system eligible qualify residents
facts.t: GESY, the state healthcare system, is for legal residents: EU citizens who work or are self-employed here or hold permanent residence or an S1, and non-EU residents with the right permit. Tourists aren't covered and use their EHIC or GHIC.

facts.q: living resident expat gesy register registration personal doctor gp portal
facts.t: Register as a resident first, then create a GESY account on the GHS Beneficiary Portal or in person at a doctor, and choose a GESY personal doctor. You need both to use state healthcare. If you work here you also register with Social Insurance, and if you have an S1 you register it with GESY.

facts.q: living resident expat gesy cost costs copayment co-payment doctor specialist prescription a&e free
facts.t: GESY isn't free. Co-payments are €1 per prescribed medicine, €6 for a specialist with a GP referral, €25 without one and €10 at A&E. You get a set number of free GP visits a year depending on your age, then up to €15 a visit.

facts.q: living resident expat driving licence license uk british exchange swap six months
facts.t: UK residents can drive on a UK licence for up to 6 months, then must exchange it, with no test. Apply early because processing takes time. An International Driving Permit does not replace the exchange.

facts.q: living resident expat driving licence license eu exchange
facts.t: EU licences are recognised, so most EU residents don't need to exchange them. You must exchange if it's lost, stolen or damaged, or after certain traffic offences.

facts.q: living resident expat driving licence license exchange how where fee road transport department tom
facts.t: Exchange a licence at the Road Transport Department or a Citizen Service Centre with form TOM 7D, a photo, ID, proof of residence and your original licence. The fee is €40.

facts.q: living resident expat electricity eac bill bills name tenant transfer account utilities
facts.t: To put the electricity in your name, apply on the EAC Portal or at an EAC customer centre. Bring your title deed, tenancy or sale agreement, ID, the previous customer's written consent (or a solemn declaration), and a bill or the meter number. Tenants pay a deposit when signing, and the transfer charge is €15 plus VAT.

src.t: Electricity Authority of Cyprus: change of tenant

facts.q: living resident expat school schools public free children kids education language greek
facts.t: Public schools are free from age 5 to 18 and compulsory from 5 to 15. Lessons are in Greek, with English taught from the first year.

facts.q: living resident expat school enrol enrolment register secondary where documents district
facts.t: Parents enrol a child at a public school in the district where the family lives. Children who don't speak Greek can join the Ministry of Education's Greek language courses and, where needed, transition reception classes.
